content: AI slop = synthetic output with superficial competence but no verification/context/responsibility; it looks finished and shifts cognitive burden downstream to readers/reviewers. The antidote ('accountable intelligence') is output tied to sources, judgment, ownership and consequences — distinguished not by a strippable watermark but by a human who took responsibility. Good Documentation Practice (ALCOA+) requires knowing who did the work; orgs need audit trails of model/data-source/human-oversight to stand behind output. Dominant theme: workload asymmetry — AI generates fast, humans bear the review burden. Validates internal provenance + provable HITL over a public AI-generated disclaimer, and validates unit-scoped drafting to keep review tractable.
